Images & geometry

All images show the same camera field: north up, east left; scale bar 30′. Click to enlarge. Survey images help with framing, not predicting exposure results. CDS DSS2 colour is the default; other sources are available under Image options.

Nominal sensor dimensions: 23.5 × 15.7 mm. Effective focal length: 530 × 0.9 = 477 mm. Field of view for each sensor dimension d: 2 arctan[d / (2f)]. This gives 2.82217732° × 1.88566571°. Survey requests use a tangent-plane projection and a 940 × 628 pixel rectangle with the same sensor aspect ratio. SkyView uses the tangent-plane dimensions d/f (converted to degrees) for its Size parameter; this gives the stated sky angles through the tangent projection. The optional CDS service uses the largest angular field dimension for its fov parameter.

These are nominal dimensions; the manufacturer’s pixel count and pixel pitch imply slightly different active dimensions. Real focal length, cropping and camera rotation can shift the framing slightly. Images use the same survey and histogram-equalisation setting throughout and are never individually enlarged to fit their object. Histogram equalisation makes details easier to see; brightness is not comparable between frames.

Image requests use stored J2000 coordinates, so a separate object-name lookup is not required. Centres are approximate at the catalog’s published coordinate precision. M102 explicitly uses NGC 5866. Coordinates follow the linked catalog, with M31 and M77 checked against the Ohio State Messier table. Catalog sizes may describe bright cores, cluster populations or different surface-brightness limits; they are not sharp physical boundaries. M16’s listed size is its star cluster, and M40’s is its stellar separation.

For an eyepiece comparison, the eyepiece focal length and field stop are required. This edition assumes your imaging setup.
